recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants to weaken the historical SHOULD wording to MAY, that should be handled as a new policy issue rather than as a reconciliation correction for FHIR-15779.
issue_request: FHIR-15779 asked FHIR-I to allow servers discretion when string searches ignore punctuation and non-significant whitespace, using OLeary versus O'Leary as the example. The final Published/Persuasive resolution said to add to the current description that ignoring punctuation and non-significant whitespace is appropriate too.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 281cb96e04d1a226a770e42beede9de64269b647, identified as GF#15779 / svn revision 14265, which added the punctuation and non-significant whitespace sentence to source/search.html.
additional_context: source/search.html is an active build page through source/hierarchy.xml. Later edits, including FHIR-44047, touched the same sentence editorially but did not change the rule. The originating Zulip thread matches the Jira request and bounded Jira/Zulip/Confluence searches found no later conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current string-search section says punctuation and non-significant whitespace SHOULD also be ignored, preserving the historically applied wording while retaining SHOULD-level discretion for problematic cases.

related_jiras.note: A later editorial commit touched the same sentence only to change 'e.g.' to 'e.g.,' and did not affect the FHIR-15779 rule.
